audience: Beginners: students and early-career learners who want practical data and AI skills. They watch a short vertical video with a voiceover.
existing: How retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) finds documents and uses them to answer a question
How a large language model writes a reply one token at a time
How a neural network learns to spot spam emails
How text embeddings let search find what you mean

ai_agents.title: How an AI agent gets a task done
ai_agents.idea: An assistant books a trip: it makes a plan, calls tools like search and calendar, checks each result, and tries again when a step fails

hallucination.title: Why chatbots make things up
hallucination.idea: A chatbot invents a book that does not exist because it predicts likely words and has no step that checks facts

fine_tuning.title: What fine-tuning does to a model
fine_tuning.idea: A general model reads many examples of a support team's replies and its answers shift toward that team's style

context_window.title: Why a chatbot forgets the start of a long chat
context_window.idea: A fixed-size window slides along the conversation; the earliest messages fall out of it and the model can no longer see them

vector_database.title: How a vector database finds similar items fast
vector_database.idea: Songs are points on a map grouped into neighborhoods; a search only visits the nearest neighborhood and skips the rest

attention.title: How attention lets a model know what a pronoun refers to
attention.idea: In the sentence 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired', lines of different strength link the word 'it' back to 'cat'

gradient_descent.title: How a model learns by walking downhill
gradient_descent.idea: A hiker in fog feels the slope and takes steps downhill until reaching the valley, which stands for the smallest error

overfitting.title: Memorizing versus learning
overfitting.idea: A student memorizes last year's exam answers and fails new questions; a wiggly line passes through every dot but misses new dots

decision_tree.title: How a decision tree decides
decision_tree.idea: A loan application falls through yes-or-no questions like a game of twenty questions until it lands in approve or decline

kmeans.title: How a computer groups customers by itself
kmeans.idea: Dots for shoppers scatter on a chart; three centers move toward nearby dots again and again until three groups settle

recommender.title: How an app guesses what you will watch next
recommender.idea: Two viewers liked the same films, so a film one of them loved is suggested to the other

diffusion.title: How AI draws a picture from noise
diffusion.idea: A picture of a cat is buried in static step by step; the model learns to reverse each step and starts from pure static

ab_testing.title: How an A/B test picks the better version
ab_testing.idea: Visitors are split at random between a green and a purple button; clicks are counted and the gap is checked against chance

sql_join.title: How a SQL join combines two tables
sql_join.idea: A table of students and a table of grades slide together and rows with the same student ID snap into one row

etl_pipeline.title: How raw data becomes a dashboard
etl_pipeline.idea: Messy sales files are collected, cleaned and reshaped on a conveyor belt, then loaded into one table that feeds a chart

prompt_engineering.title: Why a clear prompt gets a better answer
prompt_engineering.idea: The same request is sent twice, once vague and once with a role, context and format; the two answers are compared side by side
